- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices during downward trends or after sharp declines.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, overshooting true mean by 2–5% in consecutive days.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward corrections.
- Fails to capture mean reversion in medium-term (10–20 day) horizons; overestimates persistence of trends.
- Overconfident in high-variance periods; forecasts too tight around recent highs/lows.
- Underestimates price drops following high-forecast peaks; models “hold too long” after spikes.
- Corrective bias: if forecast > true outcome by >3%, reduce next forecast by 1–2% unless trend reversal is confirmed.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility into future; apply smoothing filter for 5–7 day moving average before forecasting.
